police.title: Police stop or questioning
rights: You have the right to remain silent (5th Amendment)
You do not have to answer questions about immigration status
You have the right to refuse a search (4th Amendment)
If not arrested, you have the right to leave
police.what_next: After a police stop, write down everything you remember as soon as possible — badge numbers, what was said, who was present. If your rights were violated, contact a civil rights attorney or the ACLU.
safety_reminders: Stay calm — panicking or arguing makes things worse
Document the officer's badge number and name afterward
You can file a complaint if your rights were violated
police.legal_help: Seek legal help if you are arrested, charged with a crime, or believe your rights were violated. Contact the ACLU or a civil rights attorney.

steps.title: Stay calm — hands visible, don't run or argue
steps.body: Keep your hands where the officer can see them. Sudden movements can escalate the situation.
steps.dont: Reach into pockets without telling the officer what you are doing

steps.title: Ask if you are free to go
steps.body: You have the right to know if you are being detained. If you are not being detained, you may leave.
steps.say: Am I being detained or am I free to go?

steps.title: Invoke your right to remain silent
steps.body: You do not have to answer questions. This right applies to everyone in the United States.
steps.say: I am exercising my right to remain silent.
steps.dont: Lie or give false information — that is a crime

steps.title: Refuse a search
steps.body: You can refuse consent to a search. The officer may still search if they have probable cause, but your refusal is on record.
steps.say: I do not consent to a search.

steps.title: If arrested, ask for a lawyer
steps.body: Once arrested, clearly state you want a lawyer and then stop talking.
steps.say: I want to speak to a lawyer.
steps.dont: Sign anything without a lawyer present

ice.title: ICE agents at your door
rights: You do not have to open the door
ICE needs a judicial warrant (signed by a judge) to enter — an I-200 administrative warrant does NOT count
You can speak through the closed door
You have the right to remain silent
ice.what_next: If ICE enters without a valid warrant, note everything and contact an immigration attorney immediately. Document badge numbers, names, and what was said. Try to have someone witness or record the encounter.
safety_reminders: Have a family safety plan prepared in advance
Know your A-number (Alien Registration Number) — keep it memorized or in a safe place
Have a trusted person outside your home who can call a lawyer on your behalf
ice.legal_help: Contact an immigration attorney immediately if ICE entered your home, detained a family member, or if you were asked to sign anything. Do not delay.

steps.title: Do not open the door
steps.body: You are not required to open the door for immigration agents without a judicial warrant signed by a judge.
steps.dont: Open the door even if they say they have a warrant — ask them to show it first

steps.title: Ask for identification and paperwork
steps.body: Agents must show their badge and any warrant. Ask them to slide it under the door or hold it up to a window.
steps.say: Who are you? Please slide your badge and paperwork under the door.

steps.title: Check the warrant carefully
steps.body: A valid warrant must be signed by a judge (not an ICE officer), have your correct name and address, and say 'Search Warrant' or 'Arrest Warrant'. An I-200 administrative warrant does not authorize entry.

steps.title: Assert your rights through the closed door
steps.body: Clearly state that you are not consenting to entry.
steps.say: I am exercising my right to remain silent and do not consent to entry.

steps.title: Call a lawyer and document everything
steps.body: Contact an immigration attorney immediately. If possible, have someone record the encounter.

workplace.title: Workplace raid
rights: You have the right to remain silent
You do not have to show documents unless you are under arrest
You have the right to speak to an attorney
Employers cannot retaliate against you for exercising your rights
workplace.what_next: If you are released, write down everything that happened immediately — who was there, what was said, badge numbers. Contact an immigration attorney or legal aid organization as soon as possible.
safety_reminders: Save a lawyer's number in your phone before anything happens
Know your rights at work — retaliation for exercising rights is illegal
Do not panic — running or resisting creates additional legal risk
workplace.legal_help: Seek legal help if you are detained, asked to sign anything, or if your employer is cooperating with ICE. Contact a labor rights attorney or immigration legal aid.

steps.title: Stay calm — do not run
steps.body: Running or fleeing during a raid can lead to additional criminal charges.
steps.dont: Run — it can result in additional charges

steps.title: Ask if you are being detained
steps.body: You have the right to know your status before answering any questions.
steps.say: Am I being detained? Am I free to go?

steps.title: Invoke your rights
steps.body: Clearly state you are remaining silent and want a lawyer.
steps.say: I am exercising my right to remain silent and want to speak to a lawyer.
steps.dont: Show documents unless you are actually under formal arrest

steps.title: Do not sign voluntary departure forms
steps.body: Form I-274 waives important rights. Never sign it without a lawyer.
steps.dont: Sign any voluntary departure forms (Form I-274) without a lawyer

steps.title: Document the encounter afterward
steps.body: As soon as you are able, write down every detail of what happened.

arrested.title: Arrested or detained
rights: You have the right to remain silent
You have the right to an attorney — if you cannot afford one, ask for a public defender
You have the right to make a phone call
You have the right to contact your country's consulate (Vienna Convention)
You cannot be punished for your race, religion, or national origin
arrested.what_next: After arrest, an immigration judge will hear your case. Do not give up your right to a hearing by signing a voluntary departure form. Contact family, a lawyer, or a legal aid organization as soon as you are allowed to make a call.
safety_reminders: Memorize your lawyer's phone number — you may not have access to your phone
Do not accept voluntary departure without speaking to a lawyer first
You have the right to contact your country's consulate — ask immediately
arrested.legal_help: Seek legal help immediately. Do not speak to anyone — officials, agents, or other detainees — about your case until a lawyer is present.

steps.title: Invoke your rights immediately
steps.body: State this clearly and then stop talking. Do not answer any questions until a lawyer is present.
steps.say: I am exercising my right to remain silent and I want a lawyer.
steps.dont: Say anything else until a lawyer is present

steps.title: Do not sign voluntary departure
steps.body: Signing a voluntary departure form gives up your right to an immigration hearing and may have long-term consequences for future applications.
steps.dont: Sign a voluntary departure or deportation form without speaking to a lawyer

steps.title: Make your phone call
steps.body: Call a lawyer, legal aid hotline, or a trusted family member.

steps.title: Give your lawyer key information
steps.body: Tell them your full name, where you are being held, and your A-number (Alien Registration Number) if you have one.

steps.title: Activate your family safety plan
steps.body: If you prepared a plan with your family in advance, tell them to activate it now.

rights.title: Legal References
rights.intro: These rights come from the U.S. Constitution and federal law. They apply to everyone in the United States, regardless of immigration status.

entries.explanation: No person shall be compelled to be a witness against themselves. This applies to everyone — citizens and non-citizens alike.

entries.right: Protection from unreasonable search and seizure
entries.explanation: The government cannot search your home, car, or person without a valid warrant or probable cause. You may refuse consent to a search.
In criminal proceedings, you have the right to an attorney. If you cannot afford one, the court must appoint a public defender.
No state shall deny any person equal protection of the laws. The Supreme Court has held this applies to all persons, regardless of immigration status.
Federal law limits ICE's authority to enter private premises. An administrative Form I-200 warrant does not authorize entry into a home — only a judicial warrant signed by a judge does.

entries.source: Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, Article 36
entries.explanation: If you are a foreign national and are arrested, you have the right to have your country's consulate notified and to communicate with consular officers.
You have the right to request voluntary departure instead of formal removal — but only if you meet certain conditions and have not waived rights by signing forms under duress.
Workers, regardless of immigration status, have the right to organize and engage in protected concerted activity. Employers cannot retaliate against workers for exercising these rights.

about.title: About This Site
about.what_body: Know Your Rights is a free public resource — not a law firm, not affiliated with any government agency. It provides plain-language guides to help immigrants and undocumented people understand their constitutional and legal rights during common encounters with law enforcement.
about.who_body: This site is for immigrants, undocumented people, mixed-status families, and anyone who wants to understand their rights.
about.disclaimer_body: This is not legal advice. Laws may change. Always consult a licensed immigration attorney for advice about your specific situation.
about.privacy_body: This site collects no data, sets no cookies, and has no tracking of any kind. Your visit is completely private.
